# Test fixtures

Every file in this folder is **synthetic** test data created for automated
tests. None of it describes real companies, people, games, or sales activity.

Rules for adding fixtures:

- Use invented names and reserved example domains (`example.com`,
  `example.org`, `example.net`, or `*.example`).
- Never copy rows from a real prospect list, CRM export, or email thread.
- Put a short note next to each recorded network fixture describing where its
  structure came from and that the content has been replaced or anonymized.

## Import fixtures (`imports/`)

Generated by `imports/make_fixtures.py` (run it from the repository root to
regenerate them):

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `messy_prospects.csv` | Semicolon-separated UTF-8 with BOM and CRLF: duplicate and blank rows, non-English names, a formula typed as text, malformed and ambiguous dates, checkmark flags, several emails in one cell, a row without a studio name |
| `sample_prospects.xlsx` | Two sheets (notes and prospects), Excel dates and booleans, a formula cell |
| `studios_tab.txt` | Tab-separated text |
| `studios_key_value.txt` | `Field: value` records separated by blank lines |
| `studios_cp1252.csv` | Windows-1252 encoded (not UTF-8) with accented names |

## Steam fixtures (`steam/`)

`store_responses.json` reproduces the structure of the public Steam
storefront responses (`/search/results?json=1`, `/api/featuredcategories`,
`/api/appdetails`) as observed in October 2026. All content is invented
(games, studios, dates, `.example` domains and addresses); no Steam data is
copied. It covers a self-published game, a game with two publishers, a DLC, a
demo that points to its full game, an unannounced release date, a quarter-only
date, missing contacts, a duplicate search listing and an unavailable app.
`tests/integration/steam_fake.py` serves it through `httpx.MockTransport`.
